summary: Observation of the evolution of an intense white light in the night sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On Sunday, December 18, 2016, at 9:05 PM, three people in a public square observed the silent movement of a very bright phenomenon in the night sky. This intense white light seemed to stop above a building and then quickly moved on. The light intensity decreased, and the UFO disappeared to the north, hidden by fog. The observation lasted approximately one minute. Only one witness account was recorded in 2017. It is likely that the witness saw a Thai lantern: the descriptions of its shape (rounded) and glow (very bright white) are consistent. The UFO arrived from the northeast, as measured by the prevailing wind that evening at 15 km/h: see the weather report on Infoclimat. The fact that the UFO did not have a regular trajectory (stopping, changing course, accelerating) resulted from the variable wind current characteristics in a valley near a major river. A weekend night (especially during the Christmas holidays) is conducive to festive events such as lantern releases. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of about thirty white light points and one orange point in the veiled night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, December 17, 2016, around 8:45 PM, three people in a parking lot observed about thirty white lights (including one orange one) moving silently across the overcast sky. A video was recorded. Only one witness statement was collected. The witness did not want the video published. It was most likely an observation of a Thai lantern release. The visual appearance in the video is consistent with this. The wind direction in Nîmes that evening (taken from the Infoclimat data) was from north to south: this corresponds to the movement of the UFOs (the camera generally observes them heading east and sees the UFOs passing from left to right). The witness's objections to this hypothesis are the disparity in trajectories between UFOs and the fact that some may join others. Nevertheless, the video shows that the UFOs do indeed follow one another in the same direction from left to right, but urban conditions can create local wind irregularities with some currents being faster than others. Finally, the video shows some less bright fixed points that are probably stars, as the cloud cover this evening, according to the Météociel report, is low (1/8) and some stars are visible at low elevations, particularly in the eastern sector (Procyon, Betelgeuse, Rigel). In the video, the moving points of light that protrude beyond the less bright or less sharp fixed points are likely lanterns passing in front of stars. The other reported peculiarity—a plume or halo around the points of light when the camera zooms in—is meaningless and purely the result of optical or video aberrations. It should be noted that this occurred on a weekend evening, which is always more conducive to festive lantern-licking events. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a red-orange light in the night sky over a weekend; photograph: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: On Saturday, December 17, 2016, around 8:45 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent movement of a very bright red-orange light in the sky. The light disappeared quickly, but the witness had time to take a photo. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness likely observed a Thai lantern. His description of what he saw with the naked eye is consistent with this observation. Furthermore, it was a weekend evening, always more conducive to the festive tradition of lantern licking. The wind speed measured on Infoclimat was low and consistent with the impression of minimal UFO activity. The strangeness noted by the witness, and likely the reason for their testimony (which was indeed well-considered, given that it came more than a month later), stems from the observation of their photograph, which shows an orange arabesque. This arabesque is a classic example of motion blur. The photo was taken with a long exposure (4 seconds), and the witness moved before the end of the exposure. The photo shows a strong central point of light corresponding to the period of stability during the exposure, followed by the motion blur effect, which generates a light intensity inversely proportional to the speed of movement (the faster the lantern passes in front of the detection pixels, the less they are "impressed"). The fact that this motion blur does not appear on the other bright points in the photo (likely stars) is explained by the fact that these points are much less bright to begin with and only manage to "impress" the detection pixels during the stable period, passing too quickly in front of the other detection pixels during the motion phase. The fact that the lantern was no longer visible in the sky after the photograph was taken is purely coincidental; the lantern had gone out. The fact that the witness described the UFO's movement through his viewfinder suggests that he then took some time to review the final photograph before looking back at the sky. The near-simultaneity between the photograph and the disappearance may not be as clear-cut, although it is certainly possible. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of a red-orange phenomenon in the form of two trails surmounted by a rectangle in the clear sky: observation of clouds illuminated by the setting sun.
description: On Sunday, December 11, 2016, at approximately 6:30-6:45 PM, a motorist observed a red-orange phenomenon in the sky, resembling two trails topped by a sort of rectangle. The UFO appeared stationary, then rose and slowly faded until it disappeared completely. The observation lasted between 3 and 5 minutes. Only one witness account was collected. The witness's initial impression (I'm thinking of an atmospheric phenomenon, but I don't have sufficient knowledge to verify it) is likely correct. It's probably clouds illuminated by the setting sun. Indeed, in the indicated direction (west or southwest of my position), the sun is setting (set at 6:45 PM, azimuth 250°) and may not have been visible to the witness (who is driving). The witness reports a clear sky, but some cloud fragments can be strongly illuminated (mirrored) by the setting sun, forming sometimes unusual orange geometric patterns (here, streaks topped with a rectangle) before finally "fading away." Venus and Mercury were shining in the sky in the direction indicated for the UFO, especially Venus (strong magnitude of -4.2) at 35° elevation. Either the witness didn't notice it (this (This can happen) or Venus was hidden by a cloud. In either case, this means the phenomenon was not seen at the 40° elevation indicated. Errors in absolute elevation measurements (without reference to a local geographic landmark) are very common. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: cloud observation.

summary: Long night observation of a luminous phenomenon through a window: observation of a reflection of an external light.
description: On November 29, 2016, around 12:20 a.m., a person got up and was intrigued by what they saw through their bathroom window. The witness noticed a flickering light that expanded and contracted, as well as a multicolored hexagonal object that sparkled above the neighbor's field of vision. The observation lasted about twenty minutes, during which some photos and videos were taken. The frightened witness woke their husband and then went back to bed. Analysis of the video, by pinpointing the lights on the glass blocks in the bathroom, definitively established that the lights observed by the witness were caused by the distortion of a light source by the corrugated glass blocks (see the investigation report). The light source has not been identified. But this is unnecessary since the strangeness is explained and does not come from the light itself. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: observation of a reflection of an external light.

summary: motorist observed a silent movement of a red light above the Gergovie plateau: a probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: On November 25, 2016, at 6:03 PM, a motorist was intrigued by the movement of a red light. He thought it was a motorized vehicle going uphill. But the light gained altitude above the Gergovie plateau before disappearing. No other witnesses were reported. The details described suggest the release of a Thai lantern. The trajectory is consistent with the wind measured in Aulnat on the Infoclimat website. This wind is highly variable but was blowing west at 6 PM and therefore capable of carrying the lantern towards the plateau. Weekends are always more conducive to such a playful or festive event, especially when it is already getting dark. This was the case at 6 PM (the witness described other lights in the falling night). Perhaps there were other lantern releases later that the witness did not have the opportunity to see. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Long observations of a green trail in the cloudy night sky: observation of a laser.
description: On Thursday, November 17, 2016, around 10 p.m., two people were intrigued by the presence of a green trail in the cloudy sky. One of the witnesses took several photographs. Two witness statements were collected. The green trail in the sky resulted from laser beams produced by the Toulouse event created by the international artist Yvette Mattern. This giant laser show, installed on the roof of the Quai des Savoirs (Science Museum) on the Allées Jules-Guesde, was illuminated from November 18 to 20, 2016, but the tests had begun well before. The website actu.cotetoulouse reports from witnesses who were surprised on the evening of November 16th, with descriptions and geographical distances from the event similar to those of the witness on November 17th. It was verified with the organizer that the tests were also present as early as November 15th. This laser was also observed by a witness who reported it to GEIPAN (LAPEYROUSE-FOSSAT case (31) 11/15/2016). This testimony and the attached photos present an identical aspect of the phenomenon, notably with this green luminous streak. The azimuth of the phenomenon in the sky (134°) indicated by witnesses is consistent with a laser firing from the Quai des Savoirs in Toulouse (located 25 km away at 155°), given the inaccuracy of a smartphone compass and the fact that the laser impact on clouds could be more than 10 km from the firing point. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: laser.

summary: Observation of the passage of a white luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of a shooting star.
description: On November 14, 2016, at 6:14 PM, a motorist observed a white light moving across the sky for approximately 10 seconds. Having previously seen shooting stars, he was surprised that it did not burn up and continued westward. No other reports were collected. The description provided perfectly matches the observation of a small, slow-moving meteor coming from the east and crossing the sky in front of the witness, heading west or southwest. It is common for a shooting star not to leave a clearly visible trail (or tail), especially when its brightness is low and retinal persistence is consequently significantly reduced. In these cases, any colors and their possible variations are often difficult to perceive. At the time of observation, the radian of the Taurid meteor shower (Southern Taurids then Northern Taurids) (in the constellation Taurus), quite close to the star Aldebaran, was located at its rising, just above the East-Northeast horizon (azimuth 70°N). The shooting stars from this shower (associated with comet 2P/Encke) are slow (~29 km/s), which makes the observation duration of about ten seconds quite plausible and therefore consistent with the witness account. This shower produces few shooting stars (<5/hour) but extends from September 10th to December 10th, with the observation occurring on only two days with the maximum (November 12th for the Northern Taurids), thus within a favorable period. It would appear that this shower can also produce bolides (fireballs) periodically. Based on its descriptive, temporal, and spatial characteristics, the observation recorded most likely corresponds to that of a meteor from this shower. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as A: shooting star.

summary: Observation of the movement of a very bright object with a round, flame-yellow base surmounted by a triangle of various colors: probable observation of LED balloons.
description: On November 7, 2016, at 12:35 a.m., a witness observed a very bright, colored phenomenon in the sky from their bedroom ("a round, flame-yellow base topped by a rather translucent blue, red, and green triangle"). The object, moving with a slight updraft, followed a trajectory of small zigzags towards the east. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness likely observed a series of helium-filled LED balloons. This movement is consistent with the prevailing wind direction, generally from west to east (see the Infoclimat website). The slight zigzag motion around a main axis is also consistent with an object carried by the wind. LED balloons can be clustered together to create various shapes and color combinations, as observed here (round plus triangle). See, for example, Reusable LED balloons for life. The flame-like appearance may result from some balloons in the cluster flashing, while others may remain lit. The partial and gradual extinction of the PAN (Population Exposure Panel) is due to the LEDs reaching the end of their lifespan. Furthermore, it was a weekend night, a time conducive to this type of festive event. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable LED balloon.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear movement of two ovoid objects reflecting sunlight: probable observation of airplanes.
description: On Monday, October 31, 2016, around 4:30 PM, several people in a veranda observed two cream-colored or white ovoid objects passing in the clear sky. The objects gradually moved away and were then hidden from the witnesses' view. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness likely saw the aircraft passing through the flight path (entering France from west to east) over Gravelines, 50 km away. The aircraft's movement gave the appearance (according to the witness's description) of passing over Boulogne and Saint-Léonard. At 4:30 PM, the sunlight was indeed behind the witness and had the unusual characteristic of reflecting almost perpendicularly off the fuselage of some of the aircraft (a mirror effect due to their orientation and heading). In this configuration, the aircraft appeared as an ovoid shape without wings, as the wing was integrated into the fuselage. The aircraft were flying at an altitude of 10 km and a distance of 50 km, appearing at an elevation of around 10°, which seems consistent with the UFO sighting in the witness's photograph. Their speed and distance varied, potentially creating the effect of two parallel horizontal lines traveling at different speeds. Given the aircraft's length of between 20 and 80 meters, the angular apertures could be on the order of 1/20 to 1/5 of that of a full moon, an aperture still sufficient to distinguish an ovoid shape. It should be noted that the witness does not live in the area and may have been surprised, whereas this aircraft sighting (even if fleeting due to the mirror-like properties of the sun) does not surprise the residents and neighbors. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable aircraft sighting.

summary: Observation and photography of three motionless black dots then forming a conical shape: extremely probable observation of an isolated group of three migratory birds.
description: On October 5, 2016, at sunrise, a witness observed three stationary black dots that moved closer together to form a conical shape. After this shape disappeared, another elongated white shape appeared in the sky and remained visible and stationary until 11:30 a.m. The witness took photographs. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon. According to the investigation report (see attached document), the working hypothesis is that the witness mistook the bird for a lone group of three migratory birds heading southeast. The witness misperceived the bird due to the poor quality of the optics used and the birds' distance, which prevented a clear distinction of their shape. The witness's testimony is weak, with little usable information provided by the witness. The questionnaire was not completed, and the police report is very brief. There are 15 photographs, but only a few were provided in their original form and could therefore be used for the case analysis. The photo analysis (particularly multi-temporal analysis with IPACO software) strengthens the hypothesis despite the initial poor quality of the photos. This case is classified as eAe, as an extremely probable observation of an isolated group of three migratory birds heading southeast; the poor quality of the optics and the distance of the birds prevented a clear distinction of their shape.

summary: Observation of the silent and rapid movement of white lights in the sky; all forming a "pick-up" triangle: observation from an airplane (Falcon at low altitude).
description: On Sunday, October 2, 2016, at 9:57 PM, a witness was on the 4th floor of his apartment. His gaze was drawn to 7 or 8 white lights identical to those of airplanes moving across the sky. One light detached itself from the group, the whole forming a small triangle. No noise was heard during the approximately 10-second observation. Only one witness statement was recorded. It is highly probable that the observation corresponds to a Falcon jet flying at a relatively low altitude (4900 m), as shown in the attached reconstruction document depicting this flight. The time and direction of the flight correspond exactly (the observation was made in UTC, which corresponds to 9:59 PM local time). The aircraft passed at its closest point, 3800 m from the witness, and was flying at an altitude of 4900 m. The angular elevation was 52° when the witness reported 15 to 30°, but this discrepancy is within the typical range for estimating angular elevation by a witness without ground references (such as "so many times the height of the roof of"). One unusual observation made by the witness is the description of a series of bright points. The length of a Falcon jet is 20 meters. The angular size of the aircraft seen at this distance (obtained from the altitude and ground distance) is 0.19 degrees, or 40% of the Moon's angular size (~0.5 degrees). We can distinguish many details (including craters and maria) on the Moon, and even a 40% portion of it. It is therefore quite possible that the witness saw the Falcon's windows, especially since they appear in greater contrast than the lunar features. The witness is more familiar with aircraft flying at higher altitudes, unable to distinguish anything other than the one to three typical lights without any alignment effect, as seen here. The witness, contacted by the investigator, confirms the angular magnitude of all the lights (that of the Moon). A more difficult-to-explain anomaly is the presence of the single point of light above the horizontal line. The strong coincidence of all the other points supports the hypothesis, given that aircraft may have specific lighting in addition to the regulatory lights (especially for non-commercial jets like this one). It should also be noted that this additional light could result from an error in perception or memory on the part of the witness. The fact that the plane's passage was silent (even though the window was open) can be explained by the presence of a southwest wind (15 to 20 km/h) blowing from Infoclimat, as reported on the website (Infoclimat), which was blocking the propagation of noise coming from the northeast (the Falcon aircraft's position). The GEIPAN records also contain numerous cases where the witness's perception of sound was masked by their focus or the unfamiliarity of the visual experience. The perception of aircraft noise a few minutes after the observation likely corresponds to the following aircraft passing to the west of the witness, which benefited from wind-borne noise (see reconstruction with the two aircraft). It should be noted that the witness does not mention the Falcon aircraft, which nevertheless passed by at the precise moment of the observation and within the witness's field of view. This also supports the Falcon hypothesis for the UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: aircraft sighting.

summary: Long observation in the cloudy sky of a luminous phenomenon rotating on itself: probable observation of a laser animation (sky rose).
description: On September 29, 2016, at approximately 10:56 PM, a witness looked at the cloudy sky and spotted a luminous phenomenon (shaped like an enormous helicopter blade) above Cauffry Park. The object appeared to rotate silently while remaining in the same position. The observation lasted between 50 and 55 minutes, after which the phenomenon disappeared abruptly. Only one witness account was recorded. This observation shares many similarities with one made at the same time 2 or 3 km away (see the case of RANTIGNY (60) 29.09.2016), leading to the same conclusions. These were most likely laser beams, emanating from a nightclub or a festive or exceptional event and reflecting off the cloud layer or the light rain (both were present that evening). Depending on atmospheric conditions, the range of a laser's effects varies greatly; it can reach tens of kilometers, which can make the phenomenon fleeting or even exceptional at a great distance from the source. GEIPAN has not identified the beam's emitter, but has several identified cases with similar effects. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a laser display (pink sky or light spots).

summary: Long observations of evolutions in the cloudy sky of rapidly swirling masses: probable observation of luminous animations of pink sky or bright spots.
description: On September 29, 2016, at 8:15 PM, a witness in his garden was intrigued by cottony masses spinning rapidly and silently in the cloudy sky. The witness called his partner and neighbor, who observed the same thing. The UFO was rotating counterclockwise. The phenomenon disappeared behind the clouds at 11:00 PM. It wasn't bright enough to be photographed. Two eyewitness accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon. It was most likely laser beams, emanating from a nightclub or a festive or exceptional event, reflecting off the cloud cover or a light rain shower (both were present that evening). The witness himself confirmed this origin, as he sometimes saw the beams of light rising from the ground towards the area in the sky where the "strange" discs had previously been located. Neighbors of the witnesses mentioned spotlights. Indeed, depending on the conditions of the air layer, one can see the patterns created (on the natural screen) or the beams alone without the patterns, or both, a bit like in a movie theater, imagining cigarette smoke (visible beams) sometimes in conjunction with the presence of the screen (patterns present or not). Depending on atmospheric conditions, the effective distance of a laser is highly variable: it can reach tens of kilometers, which can make the phenomenon fleeting or even exceptional at great distances from the emission point. GEIPAN has not identified the beam's emitter, but has several identified cases with similar effects. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: pink sky or bright spots.

summary: Observation very early in the morning of a very bright and motionless white ball very low on the horizon: observation of the star Sirius.
description: On September 2, 2016, at 5:20 a.m., a witness observed a very white and very bright sphere motionless in the sky. The observation lasted 5 to 6 minutes in the direction of Saint-Martin-d'Aout. The witness went to find another person, and the phenomenon seemed to disappear spontaneously. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness was surprised by Sirius, which happens frequently because it is a very bright white star. It is generally observed near the horizon (when it is visible), which can give the impression of a luminous sphere (optical effect and/or halo conferred by the atmosphere). In this case, the witness was looking in the direction of the star (Saint-Martin-d'Aout is in the southeast, like Sirius) and slightly above the horizontal (Sirius is at an elevation of 5 degrees). By the time the witness left to find his friend, Sirius could indeed have disappeared (angular displacement of 3 arcseconds in 10 meters) behind a cloud (the witness described a pitch-black night) or landscape features on the horizon. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Sirius sighting.

summary: Observation of the silent and successive passages of orange glows in the night sky: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness was with about thirty guests at a dinner party when, around 12:02 a.m. on Sunday, August 28, 2016, he saw an orange glow in the sky moving from south to north in complete silence. After a few minutes, a second glow appeared and followed the same path as the first. The same phenomenon repeated itself between seven and ten times, always with the same appearance, speed, and altitude. A photograph was taken. Only one witness statement was recorded. The entire event is consistent with a lantern-letting observation (see the investigation report: - the movement is consistent with the wind direction; - the appearance of the UFO, its trajectory, and its repetition are consistent; - the color analysis using the IPACO software indicates compatibility with the lantern origin; - it was a weekend night, conducive to a festive event. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: highly probable observation of Thai lanterns).

summary: Brief observation of the silent movement of three circular luminous phenomena in a triangular formation in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Friday, August 26, 2016, at 4:54 a.m., a witness on their terrace observed three luminous discs in the sky, emitting an opaque white light and moving north-south in a triangular formation. No sound was heard during the 4- to 5-second observation. Only one witness account was recorded. The description is entirely consistent with the observation of a lantern leaching (appearance, color). The trajectory corresponds to the wind direction that evening, towards the south (see the Infoclimat report). It was a night in August, a time of year conducive to festive events of this kind. The police investigation also indicated the observation of a similar luminous phenomenon during the night of August 27-28, 2016, at 1:30 a.m. See the website www.GEIPAN.fr for numerous cases of lanterns (search using the keyword: lantern). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of three orange lights in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Friday, August 26, 2016, at 10:39 PM, a witness and his wife were surprised to see three orange lights silently pass across the clear night sky from northwest to southeast. The lights were compared in size to a golf ball held at arm's length. They were positioned in a triangle and then obscured by trees. Only one witness account was recorded. The witnesses most likely saw a display of Thai lanterns. Indeed, lechers are frequent on summer evenings, especially on weekends, and it is common for them to appear as a triangle of orange lights, as described. The wind, recorded at 4 km on Météociel, is from the north, consistent with a movement, real or estimated at the observation site, from NW to SE. The reported observation duration is short (5 seconds) but the observed angular movement of the UFO in the sky is also necessarily borderline (30 or 40 degrees between the house to the south and the tall trees located to the north, about ten meters away). This remains consistent with the movement of lanterns at low altitude (50 or 100 m), given the potential for errors or uncertainties in UFO sightings: here, probably an overestimation of double (a factor of 2) or more compared to the actual wind speed (6 km/h recorded at 4 km) or the observation duration. The witness's main objection to this hypothesis stems from the feeling of having seen a solid area between the three points of light. This is also a classic observation of point lights at night: the eye fills the void! This objection is based on the observation of stars hidden during the passage. This very precise observation seems difficult to substantiate given the speed of the entire sighting, and given that it did not appear sufficiently clear or unusual for the witness to report it immediately (and not later). Consequently, the most likely explanation is that of Thai lanterns. Geipan classifies the case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a very bright object in the sky with a change of direction: probable observation of an object carried by the wind (and in particular of a child's balloon).
description: On August 23, 2016, at approximately 10:00 AM, a witness on his roof was alerted by the roofer, who pointed out a very bright object in the clear sky. This object moved towards the witnesses as it changed direction. No sound was heard. The object disappeared over the horizon. Only one witness account was collected. The witness described seeing an object carried by the wind, "a bit like a balloon in the wind, moving at an irregular speed." The unusual change in direction can be explained by the highly variable wind that day, particularly around 10:00 AM, as indicated by these reports: infoclimat Vinon and Infoclimat La Marche. The perception of high speed of this object is necessarily subjective since the witness did not recognize it and could not estimate its distance. The object should probably have been round; otherwise, its spinning in the wind would have caused glare. It could be a child's ball. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of an object carried by the wind (and in particular of a child's ball).

summary: Observation of the silent passage of colored light points with some flashing: probable observation of the passage of LED balloons.
description: On Tuesday, August 23, 2016, at approximately 9:45 PM, a family observed several luminous points silently passing across the sky. A flashing light was seen before the trees obscured the phenomenon. Only one witness account was recorded. The witnesses most likely saw LED balloons. These helium-filled balloons are luminous, with varying colors (including during their flight), and can be either steady or flashing. The description matches the characteristics found on commercial websites (such as Lacheballon). It is the summer holiday period, conducive to festive events, and above all, the observed movement (towards the NW) corresponds to the wind direction recorded at that time in the area on Infoclimat. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies case B: probable observation of the passage of LED balloons.

summary: Observation of the silent East-West passage of an incandescent orange sphere in the night sky: very probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On August 23, 2016, between 9:15 and 9:30 PM, a witness and his son, on the patio of their house, were intrigued by the silent movement of an incandescent orange sphere in the sky. The witness saw flames on the object and its surface. This "fireball," as described by the child, moved from east to west without changing direction until the witness lost sight of it. No noise or trail was observed. The sighting lasted 30 seconds. Only one witness statement was recorded. The entire event is perfectly consistent with a lantern-licking sighting (see the investigation report): - the movement corresponds to the wind direction; - the appearance, color, and brightness of the UFO are consistent; - it was a summer night, conducive to a festive event. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: highly probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the evolution in the sky of a dark, elongated object reflecting sunlight at times: very likely a paraglider's sail.
description: On August 22, 2016, in the middle of the afternoon, a technician on assignment in Plouha (22) observed a dark-colored object in the northern sky, occasionally reflecting sunlight. The object's shape reminded him of a paraglider wing, but nothing was hanging beneath it. The witness followed the object's movements in the sky and decided to photograph it, then follow it by car. The UFO moved slowly towards the northeast, making small rotations. The witness then lost sight of it. No other sightings were reported. The witness provided the investigator with the photograph taken during the observation: unfortunately, it did not show the UFO (too far away) but confirmed the time of the observation (3:28 PM). The observation was rather unusual, but nonetheless prompted the witness to report it in order to understand what he had seen. The witness is considered reliable. The investigation shows that it is very likely a paraglider from the PLOUEZAILES club, as indicated by its president. The case is consistent (0.7) and not very unusual (0.25). It is class A: probable paraglider in flight.

summary: Successive observations (with the naked eye then with a telescope) of a bright point in the night sky with movement and varied colours: observation of the star Capella.
description: witness reports that since August 22nd, he has been intrigued by a stationary luminous object in the sky, seen from several different locations. The witness sees with the naked eye a colored luminous object that moves from left to right and then returns to its position. He also distinguishes red, blue, and green colors with the naked eye and through a telescope. Other people have witnessed the phenomenon. Only one testimony has been collected. The witness saw a star. In the reported direction (N-NE), it was Capella, but the witness later reports that, in consultation with his astronomy club, he concludes that he saw Arcturus, which is due west and higher in the sky (30th parallel). Considering that the witness knows the directions from his home, GEIPAN (the French National Astronomical Society) would more likely consider Capella. This observation is interesting because it illustrates a typical illusion (acknowledged by the witness) of a star moving when one stares at it ("I noticed that it moved from left to right, then went down, then returned to its place"). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Capellla.

summary: Two nighttime observations of luminous phenomena: observation of the reentry of a small meteor followed by a probable observation of the passage of numerous LED balloons.
description: On August 21, 2016, around 11:30 PM, a witness observed a phenomenon entering the atmosphere with a white glow, but with phases of green and orange. A few minutes later, below his initial observation, he noticed a group of about twenty objects blinking at a constant rate, all ascending in the sky. The phenomenon moved silently across the sky. A neighbor also saw the phenomenon, but only one witness account was recorded. The witness observed two phenomena. The first was probably a small meteor entering the atmosphere. What seems to have caused the strangeness experienced by the witness, and the basis for the account, is the second phenomenon, which was apparently completely different from the first. This is likely a release of LED balloons from a boat at sea, rising into the sky with a wind pushing them back towards the land (the easterly wind this evening makes this possible, as shown in the weather report weather), thus creating a large display across the sky. LED balloons can display any color, blink, change color, all in a random or predefined, or even synchronized manner; all of this depends on the price. See the article on reusable LED balloons (e-life). The summer season and location are ideal for such festive events. The witness, not being a resident of the premises, was able to see this for the first time. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: LED balloons.

summary: Two observations of orange luminous phenomena at ground level in the same rural area: probable ground lights originating from a vehicle or human activities.
description: On August 17, 2016, at 5:45 a.m., a witness on his terrace was intrigued by a luminous orange phenomenon due west in a field at ground level. He observed, first with the naked eye and then with binoculars, a large, stationary, orange luminous shape accompanied by three small, aligned luminous orbs that appeared to rotate around the large glow. The witness estimated the phenomenon to be at a distance of 2 km. The observation lasted 2 to 3 minutes: the witness went to get his camera and found upon his return that the phenomenon had disappeared. Only one witness account was recorded. This observation from Peigney (52) of a ground phenomenon at 5:45 AM, on a hill located 2 km away (in the commune of Langres (52)), is not very strange, as it could be a piece of farm machinery, or even a simple vehicle (since it was on or near a road), with people moving around the vehicle with torches (the witness perceived a rotating light effect). In the official report, the witness recounts the same type of observation made on June 4, 2012, around 3:00 AM: observation of glows on the ground moving around a central glow, initially described as a flame, on the same hill (a few dozen meters away), specifying this time that there is a church nearby that can accommodate scouts. This therefore constitutes another hypothesis for the observation of August 17, 2016. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable lights on the ground from a vehicle or a campfire and from people equipped with flashlights or torches.

summary: Observation of the passage of several white and red lights forming a triangle; loud buzzing noise heard: observation of an aircraft.
description: On August 15, 2016, at approximately 12:30 a.m., a witness was surprised to see a luminous phenomenon in the clear sky: three white lights in a triangle and a red light in the center moving continuously at a very low altitude. The witness heard a loud buzzing sound. The observation lasted 10 seconds. The witness took a photograph with their cell phone, but it did not capture the sighting. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness was startled, most likely by an aircraft flying exceptionally low, perhaps a military aircraft (plane or helicopter). The aircraft is not listed on civilian aircraft tracking websites, and the request to the defense authorities was made too late (archives are accessible for one month). However, the description of three white lights with a red light in the center is quite typical of reports concerning aircraft (as these lights can be present in addition to the standard navigation lights), and it is common for witnesses not to recognize the standard lights (steady green and red plus flashing white). See the cases on the website www.geipan.fr, such as CONCHES-EN-OUCHE (27) 23/02/2016 or case [D417] from MUNSTER (68) towards COLMAR (68) 13/11/2015. Note here that the witness heard a humming sound like an aircraft engine. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as A: aircraft sighting.

summary: Observation in the sky of a very bright phenomenon that zigzags slightly; West-East trajectory: observation of the passage of the International Space Station (ISS).
description: On August 12, 2016, around 10:30 PM, a witness was stargazing and intrigued by the passage of a bright white light that seemed to zigzag slightly. The witness called their partner, who made the same observation. The phenomenon crossed the sky from west to east and then disappeared. The witness saw the International Space Station (ISS). Their observations in the sky correspond well to the ISS's trajectory, except for the disappearance, which was at a lower elevation than indicated, unless a cloud ended the observation. The end of the ISS's visibility (the end of its illumination by the sun) can seem strange, either because of its speed, or conversely, in this case, because of its slowness ("like a candle wick going out in 2 or 3 seconds"). The impression of oscillations around the trajectory, which also creates a sense of strangeness because a satellite's trajectory is regular, is a well-known phenomenon of autokinetic perception. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of the ISS's passage.

summary: Observation of changes in the night sky covered by two white lights: probable mistake with a skytracer.
description: On August 9, 2016, around 12:30 AM (not the 8th as indicated on the questionnaire), a witness in the town of Wissembourg (not Riedseltz) observed two white lights in the sky that appeared to follow each other above the clouds in circular and linear trajectories. The lights seemed to originate from above the clouds. They disappeared instantly. Only one witness statement was recorded. One hypothesis is favored: the observation of a skytracer (a light source originating from the ground and reflected by the atmosphere. See the investigation report). Numerous details of the observation strongly suggest this type of misinterpretation: lights in pursuit, rapid movements, circular tracking, repetitive movements, etc. (the witness described a circular chase and linear tracking, repeating like a game without actually being in the same place; there was a slight offset with each pass). It's worth noting that the weather was overcast, which is conducive to this type of misinterpretation. Various configurations are possible: visibility of the impacts alone, of the beams alone, or of both simultaneously. Weather conditions determine visibility and the distance of visibility, which explains the random, even fleeting, nature of these phenomena. The witness's objection to this hypothesis is twofold: - The type of movement. This can vary depending on the equipment and the objects involved. A witness cannot know all the possibilities. - The light appears to come from above the cloud and not from the ground. It is likely that the witness only has experience with impacts where upward beams are visible, thus giving the witness certainty that the illumination comes from the ground. When upward beams are not visible, one can indeed assume that the light comes from above the clouds. The witness's expression (e, these being illuminated from above, I mean that we could see part of the clouds underneath, unlike the famous disco lights where you can clearly see that the clouds are illuminated from below) indirectly reflects the somewhat diffuse nature of the spot (e, part of the clouds is below) typical of these indistinct beam impacts on clouds. A search for festivities that took place in the area of the observation site during the night of August 8-9, 2016, shows the presence of the Acropole Open Air in Surbourg (67), a party that took place in the parking lot of the Acropole venue on the evenings of August 6, 7, and 8, 2016, which is located 14 km southwest of the observation site, that is to say, in the direction of observation of the UFOs. This last festive evening was accompanied by an orchestra. It was not possible to determine whether a skytracer was used on this occasion. Consequently, the hypothesis of a skytracer observation remains only probable, due to the characteristic description, but not certain. The case is class B, probable misidentification as a skytracer.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of 2 red-orange lights in the night sky: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The phenomenon was observed from the witness's garden on a summer evening, shortly before 11:00 PM on August 7, 2016, while "watching shooting stars." Only one witness account was recorded. The witness reported a "first red/orange glow," "very bright," "oval-shaped," flying at an altitude of 45 degrees, but described by the witness as "rather low." A "second glow followed it." These "two glows followed each other, undulating slowly," "silently," "without noise," "without a trail," and with an apparent size of "4 cm at arm's length." These "two glows became smaller" and "turned toward the southwest." The "scene lasted a maximum of 30 seconds." The witness made a drawing of the UFO's movement. At the end of the steady journey, the "glows became smaller," the witness mentioning a "change of direction at the end of the journey" towards the "Southwest," "to the right of the two-story house." The witness specified "without noise" and "without trail." This latter direction, declared towards the Southwest, contradicts the witness's drawing, which indicates a direction towards the Northwest. We accept the drawing as being inherently more reliable. The weather situation recorded in Saint-Etienne-Saint-Geoirs (38), approximately 30 km east of the observation point, on August 7, 2016, indicates a light wind, less than 10 km/h, from the south starting at 11:00 PM (see the report from Météociel). The witness is "concerned" about not having "read or heard other accounts," even after "searching online about that night of August 7th." This account describes the characteristic features of Thai lanterns: a bright red/orange color, moving in a slow, undulating motion, without noise or trail. The direction of The movement (towards the Northwest) is consistent with the measured wind direction (towards the North), given that the latter is measured at 30 km. The final phase of fainter glows could correspond to the end of the candlelight illumination. Finally, it is a summer weekend evening, conducive to festive events such as lantern releases. The hypothesis of a lantern sighting is consistent with the observation and highly plausible. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of 4 luminous points in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On Saturday, August 6, 2016, at 11:05 PM, a couple in a garden were observing the sky when they saw four luminous points appear in the southwest, above a nearby building, flying silently in formation. The UFOs converged on the same point, moved vertically upwards, and then disappeared. The observation was very brief, and only one witness statement was recorded. The description of the UFO does not allow for a sufficiently plausible explanation (see the investigation report). It could suggest a laser-type light display or a swarm of insects illuminated naturally (fireflies) or artificially (city lights). However, the sky was perfectly clear, which does not support the laser-type light display hypothesis. The insect swarm hypothesis is inconsistent with the UFO's disappearance. The short duration of the observation (2 or 3 seconds) could also suggest a meteor, but the clustering of the points of light and the absence of a luminous trail do not fit well with this hypothesis. A meteor tends to fragment, not to assemble. The case is somewhat strange, but moderately so, because the explanations considered can neither be accepted with a probability greater than 50%, nor can they be completely rejected. It should be noted that the observation duration is very short (2 or 3 seconds) and that the testimony lacks precision (perhaps due to the short duration combined with the likely great distance of UFOs), particularly regarding the angular size of the UFO. Finally, the testimony is unique, whereas there was another witness (the witness's girlfriend) who only confirmed the observation (without providing a testimony) and who is described by the main witness as less intrigued than him. And that other friendly witnesses were also there to look at the sky but were not looking in that direction. The lack of information and corroboration prevents us from validating the level of strangeness of the observation. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation and photography of UFOs in the sky at sunset: airplane condensation trail.
description: On August 6, 2016, around 9:00 PM, a driver and her passenger observed two stationary luminous phenomena in the sky. The driver stopped to take two photographs with a camera. Only one witness statement was collected. The witness saw two UFOs (Unidentified Flying Objects): a luminous trail that did not move (IMG_0044) and a dark spot to the right of an airplane contrail (IMG_0045). The dark spot was not visually observed and only appears in the photograph. It is most likely a nearby insect. The visual description and the photograph of UFO1 are characteristic of an airplane contrail. Furthermore, the aircraft is clearly identified (Flightradar) as being in the typical configuration for producing very bright contrails (aircraft heading due west at sunset). The strangeness stemmed from the testimony of a UFO "stationary in the sky for 11 minutes," which could not correspond to an airplane (over such a duration, an airplane would vary at least 70 to 90 degrees in the sky). The witness, contacted by telephone, provided a very different account compared to his written statement. He saw UFO 1 while driving, then stopped and photographed UFO 1 (IMG_0044), then took photo 2 (IMG_0045). He was looking for UFO 1 in the viewfinder of photo 2 (it wasn't there because photo 2 is highly zoomed and framed elsewhere) and remembers his friend telling him that the UFO had disappeared from the sky. They then continued to watch the sky, without ever seeing UFO 1 again, and the whole thing lasted 11 minutes according to their watches. Thus, the actual observation time of UAP 1 is much shorter, let's say the time it took to stop the vehicle (400 m) and grab the camera (the witness specifies that it was readily available as she had just taken some photos), so perhaps 2 to 3 minutes. At the time of photo 1, the identified aircraft was at an elevation of around 8° or 9° (distance 70 km). Three minutes earlier, it was at an elevation of 4° or 5° (distance 115 km). This angular variation is small enough to be perceived as immobility, especially when the observation is not continuous. The disappearance of the UAP is perfectly explained by its entry into darkness (end of its direct illumination by the setting sun). GEIPAN classifies the case as A: aircraft condensation trail. This testimony illustrates the imprecision, or exaggeration ("immobility for 11 minutes" "These 2 phenomena, we observed them for exactly 11 minutes"), which can taint the description of an observation, often without the witness's knowledge, particularly in a context of emotion or excitement ("Heartbeats, excitement").

summary: Observation and photography of the silent movement of two luminous yellow objects: observation of Thai lanterns and a photographic artifact on a photograph.
description: On August 3, 2016, at 11:06 PM, a witness and his partner observed the slow and silent movement of two luminous objects (sunflower yellow) following one another. One of the witnesses took a photograph with his camera. The objects moved away towards the south. They disappeared, leaving only a red dot visible beforehand. The photograph, transferred to the computer, intrigued them. Only one witness account was collected. The witness experienced two strange occurrences: first, with a UFO seen with his own eyes in the sky, and second, even more striking, with the photograph. The visual observation clearly indicates a flight of Thai lanterns: this is supported by characteristics such as the color, the trajectory (corresponding to the wind speed recorded that evening: 300°, while the witness placed the UFO's arrival at 330°), the manner of final extinction, the cylindrical shape (like a "shinbone"), as well as the date, a summer evening. The surprising effect of the photograph (showing luminous flagella around the UFO) is due to a photographic artifact. The photographer left everything on automatic (flash "on" and exposure time of 1 second), triggered the shutter, and the flash immediately emitted. The flash stopped very quickly as soon as the light level needed to capture the darker parts of the frame (the tree branches) was reached, but the exposure continued for the full second for the brighter elements in the frame (here, the lantern) which didn't require a flash to be captured. Thinking the exposure was over (it's easy to confuse the near-instantaneous flash duration with the longer exposure time), the photographer stopped framing the shot and moved, with the shutter still open, resulting in these zigzags or light flagella. In this extended exposure after the flash stopped, the dark areas no longer register on the sensor and remain frozen in the state they were at the end of the flash. This is why the witness might think their camera didn't move because the tree branches are sharp, whereas it did move, which is why the lantern was captured. This testimony illustrates the potentially deceptive nature of Thai lanterns, and even more so of photographs. It also illustrates the chain of erroneous interpretations that surprise or emotion can trigger. Here, the camera malfunction and its timing error are experienced and described as linked to the strange phenomenon in the sky. The origin of the UFO is a Thai lantern, but the key element of the strangeness experienced by the witness is the photograph itself; GEIPAN classifies the case as A: photographic artifact.

summary: Observation of a very bright orange point at low altitude in a cloudy sky; spreading out lengthwise and in the shape of an inverted "L": mistaken for the Moon.
description: On July 30, 2016, at 4:15 a.m., a witness closing his shutters observed a large, very bright orange point approximately 20 to 25 arcseconds above the horizon in the cloudy sky. He initially thought it was a forest fire, then considered atmospheric reentry. His observation lasted 2 to 3 minutes before the phenomenon gradually disappeared, spreading out lengthwise in the shape of an inverted "L". Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness was surprised by the moon, which occurs when the moon is low and partially visible between the clouds; the observed luminous shape is then that of the gap between the clouds, in this case, an inverted L. The reconstruction based on the witness's drawing on a photograph and the star chart leaves no room for doubt. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: mistaken for the moon.

summary: Observation of the movement of numerous luminous points in a "V" formation in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 28, 2016, between 1:10 and 1:14 AM, a witness opened his window and glimpsed several bright points of light, forming a sort of "V" shape, moving rapidly for a few seconds. He initially thought they were birds illuminated from below, then fighter jets, but noticed no noise. The white-yellow points vanished into the night. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation likely corresponds to a flight of Thai lanterns: - glows "like stars," except that a size could be perceived as evolving (it diminished here, probably because the lanterns were moving apart). - a flight in formation (the lanterns moved within the same wind current). - a sudden pitch up and disappearance: the lanterns often go out simultaneously and can cause a change in trajectory. - The wind measured in Lyon last night (according to Infoclimat) originated from the west. The evolution of the UFO in the sky indicates a movement towards the east (therefore consistent with the measured wind) and also towards the north, as UFOs move away from the observer facing north (decrease in angular size and lower elevation or height in the sky). It should be noted that the observation took place in the city and very close to a large river, factors conducive to local wind variations compared to those measured at weather stations even if only a few kilometers away. - The observation took place on a summer night, a time conducive to festive lantern-licking events. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of a spherical object surrounded by a ring and reflecting the sun: mistaken for a passenger plane.
description: On July 26, 2016, at approximately 7:14 PM, a witness on their outdoor terrace observed the rapid and silent movement of a spherical object with a ring, moving from the north-northeast. The object reflected the sun. No trail was observed. The witness was surprised as they did not recognize any known type of aircraft (airplane, weather balloon). Following measurements taken on site, an interview with the witness, and further investigations, including Flightradar replay and meteorological archives, it can be concluded that this was a case of mistaken identity with an airplane (see the investigation report). Indeed, there was a simultaneous occurrence (within a minute) of an aircraft unnoticed by the witness at the time of the observation, following a trajectory consistent with that given by the witness for the UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon), apart from a significant difference in angular altitude (aircraft at 56°, UAP estimated at 32°), but not a disqualifying one given that the observation took place in open sky and without any reference points. An aircraft is not necessarily accompanied by a contrail. The other unusual element, concerning the spherical shape and the ring, is consistent with a non-uniform mirroring effect of sunlight along the entire length of the fuselage, and the partial visibility of the wings due to the geometric configuration (and a less favorable mirroring effect on the wings). This unusual feature could also have led to a perception of increased size compared to what is usually perceived by witnesses of passing aircraft. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies it as A: mistaken for a passenger plane.

summary: Observation in the night sky of a very bright white light: astronomical observation.
description: On July 13, 2016, at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness observed a very bright white light stationary in the southwestern clear night sky for 30 seconds. Only one witness report was collected. The witness is the same as the one who reported the sighting in Saintes (17) on March 21, 2016 (mistaken for Jupiter near the Moon). This time, the witness again mistook the light for a celestial body, either Mars or Saturn, both located just to the left of the Moon. All three celestial bodies were at low elevation that evening. The configuration of the location (as drawn by the witness) is consistent with the visibility of only one of the three celestial bodies, in the indicated direction, with the other two obscured by obstacles (a tree to the right of the UFO, a building to the left). If visible, the Moon would likely have been reported as being in its first quarter. The UFO's disappearance after 30 seconds may have been caused by the passage of a cloud. The initial impression of tremendous speed stems from the witness's perception of an object disappearing as it suddenly moves away. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: astronomical observation.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a circular orange object which changes shape and color after a change of direction: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On July 9, 2016, at approximately 10:45 PM, a witness and his wife observed a circular, orange object moving silently beneath the cloud cover for three minutes. The object became cylindrical and black after changing direction. The object was observed first with the naked eye and then with binoculars. Only one witness account was recorded. The description strongly suggests a Thai lantern flight, based on its color and appearance, the type of movement, its consistency with the prevailing wind direction (northeast wind recorded at Senebret, 9 km away), and also the final stage of the lantern's extinction, where the bright light gives way to the dark color of the lantern's body. In particular, the lantern appeared as an orange disc when viewed at close range, and later, from a more profile view, as a vertical cylinder (the exact shape of a lantern, in this case a dark cylinder because the lantern was extinguished). The non-uniform appearance of the glow within the sphere or disc, particularly when observed through binoculars, is also typical of a lantern. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies it as B: probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the successive appearance of red-orange and yellow luminous points and their movement in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 3, 2016, around 1:00 AM, a witness in a parking lot observed the successive appearance and then silent movement of several irregularly shaped, oval-shaped objects, particularly bright red, yellow, and orange in color, against a clear, starry sky. The witness was frightened by these objects, which seemed to be approaching each other. These objects disappeared, hidden by the landscape. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness likely observed Thai lanterns, which he was unable to identify due to a lack of experience with this type of observation. The testimony is weak, with little usable data collected. In particular, it lacks details about the movement of the UFOs, their trajectory, and final orientation. Nevertheless, video and photo analysis supports this hypothesis (see the investigation report). This case is classified as Be, a probable observation of a group of three Thai lanterns moving with the wind and released during a local festival.

summary: Observation of a glow coming from an object rotating on itself in an irregular upward trajectory: very likely observation of a fancy Mylar balloon carried by the wind.
description: On Monday, June 27, 2016, at approximately 9:00 PM, a witness was intrigued by a glow emanating from an object moving upwards in the sky. The object rotated on its axis without a regular trajectory. The witness took photographs. The object eventually disappeared into the clouds. Only one witness statement was collected. The statement was consistent, providing sufficient and usable data. Seven photographs also exist, some of which were used in the case analysis (see the investigation report). A thorough analysis combining meteorological data (wind, cloud cover) and processing of the witness's photographs (photo analysis using IPACO software) established that the observation most likely involved a novelty Mylar balloon moving with the wind. The witness was unable to identify it, probably having never observed anything like it before or not under similar conditions. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as eAe, as a very probable observation of a fancy Mylar balloon of a length of 1m to 2m carried away by the wind.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent passage of a red/orange luminous point and disappearance behind the trees of a forest: observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On June 26, 2016, around midnight to 12:15 a.m., a witness observed a red/orange light moving silently across the sky from their west-facing window. The light moved slowly and silently in a northwesterly direction before being obscured by trees. The sighting lasted between one and two minutes. Only one witness account was recorded in this town. The police investigation revealed another sighting of about thirty lights that same evening, within the same time frame, in Nanteuil-la-Forêt (51), a location far from the witness's observation site. This confirms the practice of lantern licking during this summer period in various parts of France. The witness's observation is characteristic of a Thai lantern, in terms of color, shape, and trajectory. The witness, looking west, described a slow, northward movement: "It was moving at low speed," "about 1 to 2 minutes before this light moved to the right." This is consistent with the wind speed measured at 3 km in Hohrod (68) (see the Infoclimat report), which was northerly and 3 km/h. The fact that it occurred on a weekend night, a time conducive to festive events, reinforces this hypothesis. A licking of numerous night lanterns is spectacular but very expensive: the use of a single lantern also remains very common, particularly by individuals. Private parties are difficult to detect because those responsible for licking lanterns do not always register with the authorities (town hall, prefecture). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of yellow-red luminous phenomena in the night sky: lack of reliable information.
description: On June 25th, at 12:13 AM and then at 12:14 AM, two witnesses on their terrace observed the movement of luminous, round, yellow-red objects that appeared successively. No noise was noticed. They quickly disappeared into the sky. Only one witness statement was recorded. This statement was given to the police by only one of the witnesses, who partially recounted observations made solely by his wife. This witness never responded to GEIPAN's request to complete a questionnaire, particularly not by his wife. Let's note the elements of the testimony extracted from the police report: - Sporadic appearance of the UFOs. - Predominantly yellow and red color. - Linear trajectory. - Immobility for each of the two sequences of approximately 5 seconds. - Observation duration of 4 seconds (Note: not consistent with the immobility duration noted above, which is longer) for the first sequence, then between 15 and 20 seconds for the second. - Very bright UFO. - Observation towards the Southeast (Note: for which sequence?). Also noteworthy is the inclusion in the report of a photograph showing a circular, white luminous phenomenon, without any mention of whether this image is related to the observation. As it stands, some of this data could correspond to several distinct known phenomena (satellite, meteor, airplane, or helicopter). However, information is missing to confirm or refute either of these hypotheses, and in particular: - Was the trajectory consistently linear? - Although the observation azimuth is known thanks to cross-referencing carried out by the Gendarmerie, we do not know if this azimuth relates to one or the other of the sequences, or both. - Altitude data above the horizon is also missing. Finally, there is doubt regarding the duration of observation and immobilization of the UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomena), mentioned twice by the witness in the contradictory official report. The testimony of the main witness's wife would also have been useful to add to the file, but was never provided despite repeated requests from GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group). The lack of information and the inconsistency of the testimony (particularly due to numerous indirect testimonies and the failure to respond to GEIPAN's request for further information) preclude its use. The case is classified as Class C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of a bright red point passing across the night sky: lack of information.
description: On Wednesday, June 22nd, at 11:15 PM, a witness was intrigued by a persistent noise coming from the garden. He looked up at the sky and saw a red dot moving across it. The dot did not blink and moved quickly. The witness filmed the object. This testimony is supported by little information; the questionnaire was only partially completed, and the video mentioned was not provided, despite repeated requests from GEIPAN. Given the limited information, the observation does not seem strange, as it could correspond to several explanations, including the release of a Thai lantern. However, in its current state, it is not possible to draw any conclusions. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies it as C: lack of information.

summary: Successive observations of the silent movement of luminous orange balls in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On June 14, 2016, at 10:35 PM, a witness in their garden observed several luminous orange orbs moving silently past before disappearing to the southeast. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness likely saw Thai lanterns. The shape, color, configuration, and trajectory in the sky indicate a lantern release, especially since the direction of movement of the orbs recorded that evening at the location is exactly that of the wind from a heading of 130°-140° (see Infoclimat). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the event as category B: probable Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a large white cloudy dot with a white trail: lack of information.
description: On Monday, June 6, 2016, at approximately 9:30 PM, a witness observed a large, cloudy white dot with a white trail for over 10 minutes. Viewed through binoculars, this object appeared to be composed of several dozen smaller objects. This white dot eventually faded and disappeared completely. The witness's description does not initially seem particularly unusual; it could correspond to one or more aircraft. This was, in fact, his initial interpretation of the phenomenon, and there was a close conjunction of aircraft in the SSE (Southeast Southeast). However, GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group) is unable to investigate this hypothesis further, or any other, because the witness did not respond to GEIPAN's requests for additional information (the UFO's altitude) or to report to the gendarmerie (French National Gendarmerie) as required by the protocol between the gendarmerie and GEIPAN. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of information.

summary: Observation in the sky of a dark line going from the ground to the sky: observation of the volumetric shadow seen edge-on produced by an airplane condensation trail in front of the sun.
description: On May 27, 2016, at 4:26 PM, a witness lying on Salins beach was intrigued by a peculiar phenomenon in the sky, crossed by an airplane contrail. The witness described a straight, black or very dark gray shape resembling a "kind of smoke curtain," visible from the ground to the sky. The phenomenon was stationary. The witness heard no unusual noises. He filmed the phenomenon. Only one witness statement was collected. Analysis of the witness's testimony, photographs, and video indicates that the strange nature of the observation resulted from a natural phenomenon known as an edge shadow. This phenomenon occurs and becomes visible when a straight airplane contrail passes in front of the sun and there is an alignment of the sun, contrail, and observer. Consequently, a shadow appears across the entire volume of atmosphere contained within the planar slice delimited by the contrail, the observer, and the sun (see the investigation report). This atmospheric slice behaves like a slightly tinted pane of glass, imperceptible when viewed head-on but forming a dark line when viewed from the side (or edge-on). This line is darker the longer the pane, meaning that the straight portion of the contrail is longer. As soon as the observer is not located within this slice, the dark appearance disappears, and the phenomenon itself. This phenomenon therefore requires specific conditions, all of which were met in this case for the witness. The resulting dark line is present along the witness's entire line of sight, including the sky. A witness who notices the aircraft's contrail in the sky might imagine the direct (or classic) shadow cast on the ground by this contrail, but much less so a shadow on the sky. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: aircraft contrail, volumetric shadow seen edge-on.

summary: Observation of the slow SN movement of six luminous orange balls in the night sky; sudden extinction of 5 balls: observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 21, 2016, at 11:45 PM, a couple in a car observed, first while driving and then while parked, six luminous orange orbs moving slowly above a nearby castle. Two orbs moved independently, one in front and the other behind the group of four remaining orbs, which formed a parallelogram. All the orbs moved along a south-north trajectory. The first orb gradually disappeared behind a cloud, and the other five orbs vanished suddenly. No sound was heard. No other witness statements were collected. The witness's observation is characteristic of a Thai lantern lecher, in terms of colors, shapes, trajectory, and even the lantern's extinction at the end of its lifespan. The fact that it occurred on a weekend night, a time conducive to festive events, reinforces this hypothesis. The witness described a movement from South to North, which is consistent with the wind direction measured at several stations 20 km away (see the Infoclimat report). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the evolution in the night sky of three orange lights forming a triangle: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 15, 2016, at approximately 12:30 a.m., a witness walking his dog spotted three orange lights in the sky at low altitude, arranged in a triangle. The lights remained motionless and flashed every other second. The first light disappeared, while the second and third rose very quickly and also vanished. Only one witness account was recorded. The appearance of three orange-red orbs on a weekend evening suggests the release of sky lanterns (known as Chinese or Thai lanterns) following a wedding or private party (see the investigation report). The witness was looking roughly south, and the objects moved from his left to his right, from northeast to southwest. The wind was blowing from the 233rd parallel (southwest), consistent with the direction taken by these lights (see the meteorological report). One of the lights rose before disappearing. The described shape is consistent with a Chinese lantern, as is the color (orange then red). The witness's description of "brightening every other second" accurately reflects a flickering of the flames. The fact that one of the "spheres" rises towards the clouds is also consistent, since, with an updraft and a lack of wind (between the houses), the lanterns can give the illusion of moving inconsistently with the prevailing wind, as evidenced by numerous videos online. The fact that another sphere then follows the same path confirms the phenomenon of wind drift. GEIPAN concludes: observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Multiple observations of the silent passage of luminous yellow-orange balls in the night sky: probably Thai lanterns.
description: On May 15, 2016, between 10:30 and 11:00 PM, several people in a garden observed the slow passage of several luminous yellow-orange balls or spheres. All the balls moved in the same direction (east-west) with regular spacing. No noise was heard throughout the observation. A video and photos were taken. The witnesses reported their observations to the police. GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group) does not have the photos and video. The statements of the four witnesses are consistent and highly characteristic of an observation of a Thai lantern release, in terms of colors, shapes, trajectory, and even the manner of disappearance, with the lanterns going out, which can create the impression of a "flash" or sudden disappearance. The fact that it occurred on a weekend night, a time conducive to festive events, reinforces this hypothesis. We do not have local wind measurements; the wind measured at 20 km is weak (5 km/h) and fluctuating in direction. The lanterns' movement could therefore be on the order of 100 meters per minute; they are actually flying much lower (100 or 200 meters) than witnesses can imagine, as they cannot accurately judge the distance to an unrecognized phenomenon. Thus, in 5 or 10 minutes, the movement across the sky can be very significant, as has been reported, even with a light wind. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations on different occasions during the same night of the evolutions of a luminous phenomenon: very probable mistake between a satellite and the planet Jupiter.
description: On April 28, 2016, between 9:06 PM and 9:30 PM, and again around midnight, two people were bivouacking at the summit of Puy-de-Tourettes. Settled in their sleeping bags in a sinkhole, the witnesses observed a bright point of light the size of a large star. They were intrigued by the way this point moved. The witness provided two photographs, unfortunately of very little use due to significant camera shake (photos taken handheld). Given the strong and consistent nature of the case (two witnesses, photos, but a lack of detail in the testimony), this appears to be a very likely case of mistaken identity involving the planet Jupiter, combined with a prior observation of a satellite in a twilight sky. The witnesses' confusion led them to conflate the two observations into that of a single object. (See the investigation report). Numerous details suggest a possible misidentification of Jupiter: a similar description, a shift in the sky during the night, apparent immobility during the observation for nearly 30 minutes, and, most importantly, the UFO's positioning similar to that of Jupiter. The witness even indicated that the UFO's disappearance had revealed Jupiter's position, previously obscured by it. However, it should be noted that the witness misinterpreted their observation, stating that Jupiter was not visible to the naked eye before 9:30 PM, when visibility conditions were perfect: a completely clear sky and a more transparent atmosphere due to the mountainous location. In any case, Jupiter was perfectly visible at the beginning of the observation period. This misinterpretation is primarily due to the witness using the appearance of Jupiter in the sky the following day as a reference point, under a flat sky and with deteriorating weather conditions compared to the previous day. The first phase of the observation strongly suggests the passage of a bright satellite, which is very difficult to identify due to the lack of precision in the testimony. However, several satellites passed over this area of the sky near Jupiter at that time, which could have caused such a misinterpretation. The various jerky movements observed in the UFO are quite typical of an optical illusion caused by involuntary eye movements (nystagmus). The case is Class B, a very probable case of mistaking a satellite for the planet Jupiter.

summary: Observation of a flash followed by a white trail with green matter at its end in the night sky and clearing; movement towards the sea: observation of a meteor.
