description: On April 20, 2016, at approximately 2:50 a.m., a motorist on the D786 before La Couture (Erquy, Côtes-d'Armor) was startled by a flash in the clear sky and then observed a large white trail with a green substance at its tip. The observation of the object, which was heading towards the sea, lasted three seconds. No other witnesses reported seeing it. As the witness suspected, it was indeed a meteor sighting, an observation reported in several locations in Normandy and Paris. See the website IMO (International Meteor Organization). GEIPAN classifies this case as A: meteor sighting.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a faint orange-white glow in the night sky: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: On April 19, 2016, at 3:56 a.m., a witness observed a SE-NW passage in the sky through a window, accompanied by a glow. Passing directly overhead, the witness described a white-orange sphere with an orange halo around its edges. Faint, it moved silently without leaving a trail. The observation lasted 5 seconds before the witness lost sight of it. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The witness's description is very precise, especially with the accompanying drawing (not provided to GEIPAN but posted on a website) in which the witness reconstructs the trajectory across the observation window. The description is entirely consistent with that of a Thai lantern flight (color, shape, trajectory according to the local easterly wind) (see the investigation report). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observations of the passage of a polygonal and scintillating object in the sky; rotation on its transverse axis: probable observations of a light debris (origin unknown).
description: On April 18, 2016, at approximately 5:40 PM, two witnesses (T1 and T2) at a bus stop observed a rotating and shimmering object in the sky. Both witnesses described the UFO as square-shaped. T1 estimated the UFO's trajectory to be straight, while T2 described it as descending. T1 filmed the observation. The observation lasted approximately two minutes for T1 and 13 minutes for T2. Both witnesses suspected it was debris that had fallen from an aircraft. No other witness statements were collected. The strangeness of this case is low and is primarily attributed to the UFO's regular rotation on its transverse axis (see the investigation report). The witnesses observed two objects. The data provided by the witnesses is extensive and detailed, but of limited reliability. The witnesses themselves describe difficult observation conditions (e.g., we were poorly positioned to judge e, a. the sun preventing us from clearly distinguishing the UFO, which was therefore only visible through the flash of white light it occasionally reflected in direction e), which may also have led to discrepancies or contradictions in the trajectory descriptions. Fortunately, we have a video of object Ne 2, on which we base the bulk of our analysis, considering that nothing in the statements precludes object 1 from having the same explanation. The physical and dynamic characteristics of the UFO observed and filmed (for object 2) by witnesses are similar to those of lightweight debris, subject to the combined effects of gravity and rotation of unknown initial cause and/or created by the general wind or its local turbulence (this being an urban environment), combined with a favorable shape effect of the object (asymmetry, propeller effect, etc.). The object's descent itself creates a relative wind that could create or contribute to this rotation, as the witness's drawing indicates a horizontal axis of rotation. This same rotation and the induced lift and drag effects could cause the deviation of 20 to 40 degrees from the wind's trajectory. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as a Be as a probable observation of lightweight debris (origin unknown).

summary: Observation of a bright object in the night sky with a particular scintillation and disappearance: astronomical misinterpretation (Sirius).
description: On Sunday, April 17, 2016, around 9:12 PM, a couple was intrigued by the presence in the clear sky of a round, bright object with a peculiar, multi-colored twinkling. The Moon was visible to the left of the object, as well as another very bright star. A witness took a video (this video was temporarily removed from the publication due to a technical problem). The witnesses looked at the sky again around 10:25 PM, but the object had disappeared. A coworker reportedly saw the same thing. Only one witness account was collected. The case is well-documented (photo, video) and of low strangeness. The description of the phenomenon, "a pinhead," as well as the twinkling, corresponds to that of a star. The witness was surprised by Sirius, which often happens. Sirius (El 17th, Az 214th) was located in a direction consistent with the witness's description, which was based on their location relative to the rooftop opposite (photo and sketch). The color changes can be explained by atmospheric turbulence. Witnesses noted that, contrary to the phenomenon that intrigued them, the star near the moon did not twinkle, which is correct since it was Jupiter and the effect of turbulence is not perceptible on planets (see the following article: scintillation). The movements in a straight line from left to right, and back and forth, are quite typical when observing a star. This is the autokinetic effect. The witness confirms that these movements remained of small magnitude. The lack of disconnection from a visual reference (the opposite rooftop) reduces the possibility of autokinetic flight, but does not rule it out. Mistaking it for the ISS is highly unlikely. Indeed, the aircraft the witness saw above the UFO has been identified, and the time it passed in the direction of the UFO is later than the station's disappearance. The hypothesis of a Procyon sighting can be eliminated. The discrepancy from the UFO sighting above the roof is too significant, and, more importantly, the aircraft was seen above the UFO even though its elevation (which can be accurately determined to the nearest 20th) is lower than Procyon's. Sirius is indeed visible lower than the aircraft and attracts more attention and leads to more misinterpretations than Procyon (because it is much brighter, more susceptible to color changes and twinkling due to its lower elevation). At 10:25 PM, when they went back outside, the witnesses observed that the phenomenon was no longer present. This can be explained by the presence of a cloud (present that day) in front of the star, and even more certainly, regarding the Sirius hypothesis, by its disappearance behind the roof (when the star's elevation was 9th). Among these several hypotheses, Sirius stands out as a very strong one. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: mistaken for Sirius.

summary: Observation of a static black ring in the sky: certain observation of a smoke ring phenomenon created by pyrotechnic tests carried out on the day of the observation at the Valbonne military camp.
description: On April 14, 2016, a witness, a farmer by profession, left his home accompanied by his father to work on his land near the hamlet of Proulieu (01). The sighting began at 9:50 a.m. as the witnesses were traveling in their vehicle, at approximately 30 km/h, on a dirt track alongside the old Blyes road (01). The weather was fine with a light breeze and a temperature of 16°C. The witness's father was the first to see the UFO, which he pointed out to his son. The UFO appeared as a stationary black ring, located, according to the witnesses, above a wooded area at an estimated distance of about 500 meters. The witness estimated it to be to the southwest, in the direction of the town of Saint-Vulbas (01). He quickly grabbed his mobile phone to film and photograph the UFO from the lowered passenger window for approximately 2 to 2.5 minutes, while continuing to drive along the dirt road. The UFO eventually disappeared, disintegrating like a small cloud. The Gendarmerie investigation revealed that this event was the subject of an article in the Sunday, April 18, 2016 edition of the newspaper Le Progrès, La Cétière edition. This article indicated that other witnesses had also seen the event. Furthermore, it was noted that on the day of the sighting, a civilian company had conducted explosives tests at the Valbonne military camp. Only one witness statement was collected. There is little doubt that the witnesses observed a smoke ring produced by the use of pyrotechnic devices during explosive tests at the Valbonne military camp (see the investigation report). As the test site was quite far from the witnesses' location, they likely did not hear the detonations that created this black ring, or perhaps heard them later without making the connection. It should also be noted that the weather conditions were favorable for the ring's structure to persist for several minutes, as the wind was very light at the time of its formation. The strangeness of this case is minimal and stems primarily from the unusual appearance of the UFO, which the witnesses were unable to link to any phenomenon they were familiar with, having probably never observed it before. The testimony is consistent, with sufficient usable data provided by the witness, and the police report is complete and well-documented. There is also a video and six photographs, which were used for the case analysis. This case is classified as eAe, as a confirmed observation of a smoke ring phenomenon created by pyrotechnic tests carried out on the day of the observation at the Valbonne military camp.

summary: Long night observation of a luminous phenomenon of colours in the clear sky: astronomical mistake with Sirius.
description: On April 3, 2016, at 10:10 PM, a witness, standing on his doorstep, was intrigued by a bright light seen to the right of the church steeple in his village. The phenomenon emitted colored lights (blue then red). No sound was heard. The phenomenon was finally lost from sight at 10:45 PM. The witness took two photographs. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness saw Sirius. At low altitudes and under certain atmospheric conditions, Sirius's glow can vary in color and be misleading. Geometric reconstruction from the witness's photograph and the estimated location where the picture was taken reveals a coincidence within 1 or 2 degrees between Sirius and the UFO. Furthermore, the UFO's trajectory (direction and speed) as described by the witness is perfectly aligned with Sirius's trajectory. The alternative possibility of a lantern, which could very well have been launched on a Sunday evening, must be ruled out. Indeed, this would have meant that the witness did not see Sirius and that it was hidden by a cloud, whereas the witness's account indicates a clear sky. The wind on that day (infoclimat) is consistent with the direction of travel, but with an intensity (10 km/h) resulting in a much greater angular velocity at an altitude of 200 m and a distance of 600 m (calculated from the elevation), completely out of proportion with the observation (even if the wind were 10 times less intense than what the weather station a few kilometers away reported). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this observation as A: Sirius.

summary: Motorist observing a bright point in the sky followed by a black shape appearing to release material: observation of a passenger plane and intermittent contrails.
description: On March 29, 2017, at 7:19 a.m., a motorist on the A34 motorway heading towards Charleville-Mézières observed a peculiar phenomenon in the clear sky. The witness was startled by a bright point of light, and then, a short time later, observed a dark shape that could have been an aircraft. The object appeared stationary and seemed to be releasing a substance, possibly a mixture of smoke and water. The witness moved beneath the observed object and took photos and a video. He then noted a triangular shape and two large wings. A red light was present in the center of the object, which eventually disappeared from the witness's view. The observed object was identified as an A380 seen under specific conditions (Flight Number: SQ336 - SQ336 9V - SKF - Call Sign: SIA336 - Airbus A380-841 - From Singapore to CDG): see the attached investigation report. The strangeness caused by the stability or low speed of the UFO (at least during part of the observation) resulted from a pivoting effect: as the witness and the aircraft were moving in opposite directions, the line of sight between the witness and the UFO tended to pivot near a fixed point. The witness, unable to perceive the changing distance, believed the UFO was almost stationary. The witness thought that material was being poured from the UFO, when in reality it was intermittent contrails, as the aircraft was flying at altitude and encountering varying contrail formation conditions. We invite you to watch videos of contrails from an A380 by following the internet links on page 18 of the investigation report. Another strange phenomenon resulted from the UFO's varying brightness in intensity and color. The aircraft reflects sunlight (which is not visible to the observer) back towards the witness. This reflection is variable, even intermittent, depending on the aircraft's geometry (it is a specific part of the aircraft that produces the reflection). As the aircraft descends, the sun, as seen from the aircraft, approaches the horizon and becomes reddish (a rapid sunset as seen from the aircraft), and the reflection on the aircraft also changes color. All these reflection phenomena have been successfully reproduced through simulation. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of a commercial airliner.

summary: Long observation of a very bright fixed object to the left of the Moon: astronomical mistake with Jupiter.
description: On March 21, 2016, at 11:00 PM, a witness observed a very bright, round, white object in the southern sky, stationary to the left of the Moon. No unusual noise was heard. The observation, first with the naked eye and then with binoculars, lasted for an hour. The object had completely disappeared by 4:00 AM. No other reports were collected. The witness was surprised by Jupiter. This is common; the planet's appearance is much brighter than a star and does not twinkle. Although the witness described it as having a brightness comparable to the Moon and an enormous size (though still much smaller than the Moon in his drawing), there is no doubt that it was Jupiter. Indeed, the description, made over a period of five hours, of the UFO's trajectory in the sky relative to that of the Moon, as well as the witness's drawing, perfectly match the celestial configuration that night. In the reconstruction (see PPT document), we find the witness's description: the UFO is Jupiter to the left of the Moon and the star to the right of the Moon that is actually visible, is either Alphard (magnitude 1.95, to the right below, as in the diagram), or Regulus (magnitude 1.35, to the right above). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: mistaken for Jupiter.

summary: Brief observation of a flash followed by a loud noise and subsequent discovery of traces of burnt grass in a field: insufficient observational data.
description: The witness was in bed when a bright light illuminated his room, followed by a loud noise. He later noticed traces of burnt grass in a neighbor's field. No other witnesses reported seeing the sighting. The observation was extremely brief (1 second) and, crucially, consisted solely of a light and a noise perceived from his bed. The witness did not leave the house and therefore could not describe a UFO (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) with any possible shape, position, etc. The light could thus have had various origins (storm, spotlight, meteorite reentry, etc.). Furthermore, the witness found a round mark in the ground the following day. In the absence of any UFO sighting, there is no particular reason to investigate such traces in relation to a UFO, especially since round marks can have equally varied origins (examples: fairy ring mushrooms, traces of an old inflatable pool, motorcycle skid marks, etc.), and these marks may be of varying ages and could have escaped the witness's notice (they are not, moreover, in the immediate vicinity of the house) as long as they were not actively searching for them. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: insufficient observation data.

summary: Observation of a bright white point in the sky with scintillations of colors in the night sky: observation of Sirius at low altitude.
description: On March 5, 2016, around 11:00 PM, a witness was intrigued by a bright point of light that appeared stationary in the sky. He observed the phenomenon through binoculars and distinguished blue, violet, and white beams. His wife, who was also present, thought it might be a star or a twinkling planet. The witness reported the point at an azimuth of 236° (but measured indirectly using Geoportail) and an elevation of less than 15°. The witness's wife also considered it to be a star, but with a violet color. Between 11:00 PM and 11:30 PM, Sirius moved between an azimuth of 215° (SSW) at an elevation of 15° and an azimuth of 225° (SW) at an elevation of 13° (see attached star chart with Stellarium). The UAP can therefore only be Sirius; otherwise, the witness would also have reported Sirius (or a very visible star in a clear sky, especially when looking through binoculars!) in the immediate vicinity of the UAP. The main witness saw Sirius and was misled, as is typical, by Sirius's glow and changing colors at low altitude, and this may have been further exacerbated by the observation through a window. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Sirius sighting

summary: Observations by several witnesses of the low-altitude passage of a large object: observation of the passage of a C130 military aircraft.
description: On the night of February 23-24, 2016, around midnight, several people in cars were intrigued by the sight of a large object flying at very low altitude. The object had lights of different colors, some steady, some flashing. Witnesses described a circular or triangular object moving slowly across the sky at treetop level. Four witnesses gave statements to the police. It appears that witnesses T1, T2, and T3, all from the same vehicle, and the single witness observed a C130 aircraft, clearly identified (air traffic information), which took off from Air Base 105 in Évreux, heading southwest, and then passed south of Conches-en-Ouche at low altitude on a heading of approximately 210° (see the attached investigation report). This is a perfect illustration of how an airplane, in combination with other factors, can evoke fear, emotion, and even contempt, particularly when: - the airplane is unusual (a large military aircraft), causing fear for the witness in Conches-en-Ouche. The airplane was too large and flew too slowly for the witness. Indeed, we already know that Airbus A380s and A320s taking off or landing do not give the same impression of speed and altitude at all, even though everything else is identical. - An illusion of hovering occurs (for the witness driving on the RD830) resulting from a pivoting effect when both the witness and the phenomenon are moving and the axis connecting them pivots around a fixed point or area, which is then taken to be the stationary point of the phenomenon. The impression of pivoting is enhanced here by the presence of a fairly continuous foreground of trees, obscuring the view. The lighting is very unusual; here, the full moon, not directly visible, but reflected off the aircraft or diffused through the treetops, creates disc, star, and halo effects of light that can indeed contribute to the strangeness of the event. A more complete analysis is provided in the attached document, including: - the radar trajectory of the C130 aircraft; - a cartographic reconstruction of the observations showing the aircraft's trajectory, the witnesses' positions, and their direction of observation. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: mistaken for an aircraft. More generally, this case illustrates the richness and fragility of human testimony when faced with an unrecognized phenomenon, under less than ideal observation conditions, and, moreover, in a situation of heightened emotion due to the strangeness of the event. Witnesses in the same car estimate very different distances (300 m to 10 km). They see the aircraft primarily as circular or round, but with significant variations, while the witness from Conches-en-Ouche sees a triangle. The red lights may be steady or flashing, depending on the witness. The driver is certain he stopped the vehicle, while the passengers claim otherwise. One might also wonder about a possible influence effect between witnesses or an amplified sense of strangeness when a witness detects the phenomenon and points it out to others, labeling it a UFO.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a bright point in the sky; downward trajectory: observation of a bolide.
description: On Wednesday, February 17, 2016, at approximately 6:20 PM, a witness at home observed a bright point of light moving north-south through a window on a descending trajectory. The observation lasted 3 to 5 seconds. Only one witness report was collected. This fireball was seen by numerous witnesses at the same time in southern France and recorded by the IMO (International Meteor Organization). See the website IMO, which lists more than 120 reports from different regions of France. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: fireball observation.

summary: Observation of a stationary white light bar in the sky and disappearing into the clouds: lack of information.
description: On Sunday, January 31, 2016, at approximately 6:45 PM, a witness observed a cluster of white lights in the sky, resembling halogen lights and forming a stationary bar. No sound was heard. The phenomenon quickly disappeared behind a cloud. No other reports were collected for that day. The witness, after some research, discovered that a similar object had been seen in Vichy in 2012. Several aspects lend an air of mystery to this sighting: the shape (a white luminous bar approximately 5 arcseconds wide), the significant altitude (70 arcseconds), the angular immobility, and the possibility of clouds passing in front of it. Celestial bodies, airplanes, balloons, and lanterns seem unlikely explanations, leaving only the possibility of a construction helicopter carrying a beam or an illuminated ramp. The gendarmerie reported EDF (French electricity company) power line monitoring work using helicopters in the preceding days or weeks, but never on Sundays. Since the witness did not go to the police station as requested by GEIPAN and did not respond to two requests to meet with the GEIPAN investigator, it is not possible to better understand and process this testimony. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: no witness response, lack of reliable information.

summary: Observations of the rapid evolution of a green ball that splits into several luminous green balls: probable observations of the effects of a playful laser.
description: On Sunday, January 24, 2016, at approximately 12:40 a.m., a witness on his terrace saw a luminous green sphere pass by and stop in the middle of the trees. The witness went inside to get his partner, and for less than two minutes, they watched the silent evolution of the phenomenon. The sphere moved over a soccer field, then made a very rapid round trip before splitting into four smaller spheres. They disappeared behind a nearby hedge only to reappear in front of it. The four green spheres moved off towards the north-northwest at great speed. Intrigued, the witnesses went down into the street, saw no other witnesses, and never saw the phenomenon again. One of the witnesses filed a report with the police. No other reports were collected. The police indicated that a nightclub located 9 km from the town was equipped with a laser projector, which was visible within a radius of approximately 20 km. Furthermore, a wind farm was located in the area. The witnesses are reliable and do their utmost to accurately recount what they saw and experienced. Following an on-site investigation, verifications were carried out (see the investigation report). The phenomenon is not particularly strange, as it can resemble the effects (not always known and therefore potentially surprising) produced by a small green laser transmitter equipped with a few functions (emitting a wide beam, or several small beams) operated by a neighbor. The information gathered does not allow for the identification of the laser's origin (without a neighborhood survey), but the laser remains the likely cause of the phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies the case as B: recreational laser.

summary: Observation of the movement of an ovoid object in the sky: observation of a helicopter.
description: On Sunday, January 24, 2016, at approximately 12:45 PM, a witness was intrigued by the passage of a luminous, ovoid-shaped flying object over the horizon. The object disappeared as a gray dot. No unusual noises were heard during the observation. The phenomenon described by the witness suggested an aircraft, either a helicopter or a plane, despite the seemingly incompatible ovoid shape. A check of civil air traffic data using Flightradar, based on so-called "secondary" radar information, showed two unusual aircraft in the area (see the records available in the appendix): - a Beech 200 aircraft, flight reference OOLET, flying at an altitude of approximately 8,000 meters, making multiple circles above the Col de Braus. -An Ecureuil helicopter, flight 3AMAX, which the radar only detects intermittently because it is flying at an altitude of approximately 1000m, at a distance of about 10km from the witness. The 11:57 UTC (12:57 local time) record shows the two aircraft very close together, as indicated by the witness. The aircraft then makes a clear change of direction. This aeronautical activity in this sparsely populated area is unusual: a search of regional events indicates that at that moment, Special Stage 16 of the Monte Carlo Rally was taking place (see copy of the web pages in the appendix): -SS16 Start 12:08 from Col de l'Orme Finish Saint-Laurent (Power Stage) (Live TV) 12:07. This stage was broadcast live on television. For this to work, it is highly likely that the helicopter took the footage, transmitted it to the aircraft, which then transmitted it to the central TV control room. GEIPAN did not conduct any investigations to identify the various operators of the system. This type of operation is common for large, highly mobile sporting events (see this intriguing plane). The Météociel weather report from Nice: Météociel indicates a light northwesterly wind at noon, shifting to due south at 1 p.m. In both cases, the wind is unfavorable to the propagation of the helicopter's noise towards the witness. The helicopter is approximately 10 km from the witness, a sufficient distance to make it inaudible under these conditions. The witness, who only discerns an oval shape, is likely only observing the reflection of the sun on the aircraft, without being able to make out any details. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: observation of a helicopter flying over a stage of the Monte Carlo Rally.

summary: Sighting of a bright, blinking point of light passing across the sky: likely sighting of a satellite.
description: On Friday, January 15, 2016, around 6:30 PM, a witness in front of his garage scanned the sky and observed a white-orange object flashing between the stars. He ruled out the possibility of an Iridium flare due to the flashing, as well as an ISS pass. The object was quickly obscured by the house. Only one witness account was collected. The garage entrance is located in the southeast corner of the house, facing east. At the end of the observation, the UFO disappeared behind the house, hidden by the building (the object passed over the house and I could no longer see it), which confirms the direction of the UFO's disappearance, that is, towards the northwest. Given its low strangeness and moderate consistency (single witness, no photo or video), this case appears to be a likely case of mistaken identity involving a rapidly rotating satellite, perhaps in distress (see the investigation report). The observation indeed presents the characteristics of such a misidentification (see the investigation report). This type of object, relatively unknown to the general public, can be a significant source of misidentification. It should be noted that several malfunctioning satellites or rocket stages, potentially in rapid rotation, passed across the sky along the trajectory described by the witness at the time of the observation. However, the lack of detail in the witness statement, as well as doubt about the time of the observation, prevents formal identification of this satellite. This case is Class B: probable misidentification as a satellite.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of several flame-colored luminous phenomena in the New Year's Eve night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On January 1, 2016, at 12:16 AM, a witness observed the silent movement of flame-colored luminous phenomena across the sky. The objects were moving towards the NNE on a horizontal trajectory at low altitude. The observation lasted 5 minutes. No other witnesses in the area reported seeing them. The observation of orange balls or discs crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a weekend or festive night like New Year's Eve, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement in groups of 4 or 5, aligned horizontally, likely resulted from launches in quick succession, separated by longer intervals. The movement was observed towards the Northeast, while the prevailing wind in the area (8 km away) was towards the Northwest. However, from the observation point, the witness could only clearly discern the south-to-north component of the movement. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the slow, silent movement of three diamond-shaped, red-orange objects in the New Year's Eve night sky: probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: On January 1, 2016, at 12:15 AM, a driver and his passenger observed the slow, low-altitude passage of a diamond-shaped, yellow-orange object moving silently in the south-south direction. Two others were soon followed. Fireworks were being set off at the same time. No other witnesses were reported. The observation of orange balls or discs in the sky on a weekend or festive night, such as New Year's Eve (the witness also mentioned fireworks), strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The wind (Armentières weather station 3 km away) at that time was light but with a strong south-to-north component, consistent with the passage of UFOs across the road. The witness then reported the UFOs turning to follow the road. The impression of following the road does not rule out the possibility of a trajectory with a strong transverse component to the road, especially since the witness also reports that the UFO was moving slowly (in the direction of travel) and that all of this was observed while driving.
